channel.title: Pier & Point · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks (Pier 70), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: The dry docks page told readers to 'see' a field name that the page itself shows as 'Traced from', and it used two DataSF column names, for the recorded drop date and for the Assessor's secured roll. It now says 'see Traced from above', 'a recorded drop date of 2018-10-02' and 'on the Assessor's secured roll'. The page also said DataSF's record was checked on October 10, 2026; it was read on both October 10 and October 11, 2026, with the same result, and the page now says so. The earlier entry on this page about the Port's expected demolition-contract timing now opens with 'On July 15, 2026, Potrero View reported that the Port expects', so the date reads as a report, not an event. Nothing about the lot or the outline on the map changed.

item.title: Correction · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: The dry docks now sit on the two real floating hulls. Their outline had been a rough box drawn in open water north of the shipyard. The new outlines are traced by hand from satellite imagery, so they are still approximate. Which hull is Dry Dock No. 2 and which is the Eureka is matched by length and is not confirmed by a source.

item.title: Correction · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: The two dry docks sit inside Assessor lot 9900068, the lot for the whole shipyard. This record had said no lot exists, because the search used to check looked for street names. The lot's entry shows a drop date of 2018 but still reads active, and the dataset does not explain that. The outlines on the map are unchanged.

item.title: Correction · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: Dry Dock No. 2 was built in 1970; the record had also called it a 1940s dock, which is the Eureka's era. The Eureka's length is reported as 528 feet by one outlet and 570 feet by another, so both are shown. The 2027 dates for the demolition plans and contract come from Potrero View's own wording, not a quotation from the Port.

item.title: Added · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: New nearby-project record for the Piers 68 & 70 dry docks (Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock), next to Pier 70 but outside its tracked boundary. It follows the Port's December 2025 emergency declaration over Dry Dock No. 2's hull tears and listing, the January and February 2026 Port and Capital Planning Committee memos on stabilization and planned demolition, and Mission Local's February 2026 reporting on the $61.2M disposal cost.

item.title: Expected · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: Demolition contract expected to be tendered in the second half of 2027, and initial plans completed by March 2027 (the Port, as reported by Potrero View on 2026-07-15, in the article's own wording rather than a quotation). (~2027)
item.description: Demolition contract expected to be tendered in the second half of 2027, and initial plans completed by March 2027 (the Port, as reported by Potrero View on 2026-07-15, in the article's own wording rather than a quotation). (~2027). Source: Potrero View, 2026-07-15.

item.title: Milestone · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: Potrero View reports the Port has directed an outside engineering firm to prepare preliminary engineering plans for demolition of both dry docks and help secure permits; a Port spokesperson is quoted saying the package will be used "to advertise for a future design-build contract". Separately, in its own words rather than as a quotation, Potrero View says the Port expects initial plans to be completed by March 2027 and a demolition contract tendered in the second half of 2027 (the Port, as reported by Potrero View). This is later than the summer 2026 advertising the January 2026 Port memo anticipated. (~2026)

item.title: Milestone · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: Capital Planning Committee reviews a supplemental memo giving the full cost picture: $61.2M total estimated cost to stabilize and dispose of Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock, of which about $20.0M was secured and about $41.2M remained pending FY2026-27 budget approval. (Feb 9, 2026)

item.title: Milestone · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: Port Commission receives an informational memo (Calendar Item 9A) on the dry dock emergency, the stabilization work under way (continuous pumping, reinforcing steel, stabilizing deck cranes, capped at $10,000,000), and staff's plan to advertise a demolition-services contract in summer 2026. (Jan 9, 2026)
